content: The staging of neuroblastoma is determined using the International Neuroblastoma Staging System (INSS). Additionally, the International Neuroblastoma Risk Group Staging System (INRGSS) has been proposed, which classifies neuroblastoma into four stages based on the extent of disease dissemination and imaging findings. Neuroblastoma patients are stratified into three risk groups: low risk, intermediate risk, and high risk. This stratification is based on the INSS stage of the tumor, the patient’s age, tumor histology, and the amplification status of the MYCN oncogene. Low-Risk Neuroblastoma 1. Patients with stage 1 tumors are classified as low risk, regardless of age, tumor grade, or molecular characteristics. 2. Patients with stage 2A or 2B tumors that are more than 50% resected are considered low risk, irrespective of age, tumor grade, and MYCN amplification status (MYCN not amplified). 3. Patients with stage 4S tumors, stage 1 tumors, and MYCN not amplified are also included in the low-risk category. Intermediate-Risk Neuroblastoma Group 1: 1. Patients with stage 2A or 2B tumors that are less than 50% resected or biopsied only, aged 0–12 years, with MYCN not amplified, are classified as intermediate risk. 2. Patients with stage 3 tumors, aged 1 year, with MYCN not amplified, are included in this group. 3. Patients with stage 3 tumors, aged 1–12 years, with favorable histology and MYCN not amplified, are also intermediate risk. 4. Patients with symptomatic stage 4S tumors, aged 1 year, with MYCN not amplified, are included in this group. Group 2: 1. Patients with stage 3 tumors, aged less than 365 days, with unfavorable histology, a DNA index of 1, and MYCN not amplified, are classified as intermediate risk. 2. Patients with stage 4 tumors, aged 1 year, with MYCN not amplified, are included in this group. 3. Patients with stage 4S tumors, aged less than 365 days, with unfavorable histology, a DNA index of 1, and MYCN not amplified, are also intermediate risk. Group 3: 1. Patients with stage 4 tumors, aged less than 365 days, with unfavorable histology, a DNA index of 1, and MYCN not amplified, are classified as intermediate risk. 2. Patients with stage 3 tumors, aged 365–547 days, with unfavorable histology and MYCN not amplified, are included in this group. 3. Patients with stage 4 tumors, aged 365–547 days, with favorable histology, a DNA index greater than 1, and MYCN not amplified, are also intermediate risk. High-Risk Neuroblastoma 1. Patients with stage 2A, 2B, 3, 4, or 4S tumors, regardless of age or tumor grade, with MYCN amplification, are classified as high risk. 2. Patients with stage 3 tumors, aged 547 days or older, with unfavorable histology and MYCN not amplified, are included in this group. 3. Patients with stage 4 tumors, aged 365–547 days, with unfavorable histology, a DNA index of 1, and MYCN not amplified, are classified as high risk. 4. Patients with stage 4 tumors, aged greater than 547 days, regardless of tumor grade or MYCN amplification status, are also included in the high-risk category.
